findings.title: Missing fsync_directory import makes the publication-order test fail before its intended fault
findings.description: The module imports DeployError, Layout, atomic_write, mkdir, read_json, write_json only. test_transaction_parent_failure_prevents_configuration_stop_and_selection.fail calls fsync_directory for an earlier directory path and raises NameError, which assertRaises(OSError) cannot catch. The later import inside terminal_failure is function-local and cannot bind this callback. Parent separately confirmed this in the Linux targeted run. No source change made.
findings.validation: Static lexical-scope verification after reading the full file; independently executed Linux failure reported by parent, not rerun here.

notes: The known P2 missing fsync_directory import remains unfixed in the frozen source; the round is dirty. Parent Linux diagnostics are external to this read-only review and their failed tests were never counted as passes here.

No new confirmed production/documentation defect was found in the29-file continuation. Read-only historical evidence does not establish present external-account, public-HTTPS or future-ACME-renewal acceptance.

Worktree archive power-loss durability of externally unsynced content remains an unconfirmed concern separately referred to parent. Current deploy README promises whole-tree reversible move preserving ignored/dirty content, not an explicit fsync guarantee for arbitrary user writes; it is not included as a confirmed finding.
Generated lock/capability coverage uses explicitly permitted structural validation with exact limitations above; no path-only inventory entries counted as manual reading.
